When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

content.text:
Both failures diagnosed. They're unrelated to each other.

## 1. `e2e-tests (opencode)` — transient infra, not your code

Failed 15s in, at **Install agent CLI**:

```
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
→ Failed to fetch version information   (exit 1)
```

That message comes from the installer itself, which resolves the version with an **unauthenticated** call:

```bash
specific_version=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases/latest | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"v\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
if [[ $? -ne 0 || -z "$specific_version" ]]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Failed to fetch version information${NC}"; exit 1
fi
```

Unauthenticated `api.github.com` from a shared Actions runner IP gets rate-limited → empty body → bail. Evidence it's transient: the endpoint returns `200` / `v1.18.18` right now, and the opencode job passed in **all 8 prior runs** on Aug 13–14 — this is its only failure. Just rerun it. If it recurs, the installer reads `VERSION` from the env (`requested_version=${VERSION:-}`), so pinning a version skips the API call entirely.

## 2. `e2e-tests (factoryai-droid)` — real, and broken since Aug 12

`TestFactoryTaskCheckpointExistsBeforeCommit` and `TestFactoryCommittedCheckpointExcludesPreExistingUntrackedFiles`, both failing at `waitForTaskCheckpoint` ("expected task checkpoint within 30s"), both also failing on retry. **Failing in every E2E run since 2026-08-12 05:47**; last green was 2026-08-10 21:43.

Comparing `entire.log` from the last passing run against this one:

| | Aug 10 (pass) | Aug 14 (fail) |
|---|---|---|
| `pre-tool-use` → SubagentStart | 21:47:11.176 | 15:28:31.989 |
| `post-tool-use` → SubagentEnd | 21:47:38.963 (**+27.8s**) → `new_files=1` → task checkpoint saved ✅ | 15:28:35.166 (**+3.2s**) → 0 changes → *"no file changes detected, skipping task checkpoint"* ❌ |
| worker's own `stop` | 21:47:37.493 (before SubagentEnd) | 15:28:54.370 (**19s after** SubagentEnd) |

**Droid changed Worker dispatch from blocking to background.** The tmux panes confirm it directly:

- Aug 10: `Worker "Inspect code and write summary"` — a synchronous tool block
- Aug 14: `Worker launched … It will complete in the background and notify automatically.`

Droid's `PostToolUse` now fires when the *launch call returns*, not when the Worker *finishes*. Our handler at `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1198` therefore sees an unchanged worktree and skips.

The work isn't lost, but it's **misattributed**. The Worker now runs as its own full droid session (own SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop), so its file lands as an ordinary session checkpoint:

```
commit 3a5ca02 (entire/775fb1a-e3b0c4)
    # Task Tool Invocation Subagent type: worker …
    Entire-Metadata: .entire/metadata/398f4162-…      ← worker's own session
```

That's `.entire/metadata/<worker-session>/`, not `.entire/metadata/<parent>/tasks/<toolUseID>/` (`strategy/strategy.go:266`). The tests scan shadow trees for `/tasks/`, so they never match.

**So this is a product regression, not just a stale test**: for Factory AI Droid, subagent work is no longer attributed to the parent session as a task checkpoint — it surfaces as an unrelated top-level session.

My recommendation is to fix the CLI rather than relax the tests: stop keying task checkpoints off `PostToolUse` timing for droid, and instead correlate the Worker's own session back to the parent's `tool_use_id`, emitting the task checkpoint when the *worker session* ends. One thing I did not verify — worth checking before you commit to that design — is whether droid's worker `SessionStart` payload actually carries a parent-session or tool-use reference. If it doesn't, the correlation has to fall back to timing heuristics, which is fragile enough that relaxing the assertion may be the more honest option.

14	// droidSessionStart is the first line of a Droid session transcript. A session
15	// spawned by the Task tool records the invoking session and tool-use ID here;
16	// a top-level session leaves both empty.
17	type droidSessionStart struct {
18		Type             string `json:"type"`
19		CallingSessionID string `json:"callingSessionId"`
20		CallingToolUseID string `json:"callingToolUseId"`
21		SessionTitle     string `json:"sessionTitle"`
22	}

24	// sessionStartScanLimit bounds how far into a transcript we look for the
25	// session_start entry. Droid writes it first; the allowance only covers a
26	// future format that prepends a line or two, and keeps a large rollout from
27	// being read end-to-end on every turn.
28	const sessionStartScanLimit = 8
29	
30	// ResolveSubagentSession reports whether this transcript belongs to a Worker
31	// session spawned by a parent task invocation.
32	//
33	// Droid runs Workers as detached sessions: the parent's PostToolUse hook fires
34	// when the Worker is dispatched, before it has touched the worktree, so only
35	// the Worker's own session boundary can delimit its work. Its transcript's
36	// session_start line carries callingSessionId/callingToolUseId, which survives
37	// independently of hook ordering and of the synthetic tool-use IDs the CLI mints
38	// when Droid's tool hooks omit one.
39	func (f *FactoryAIDroidAgent) ResolveSubagentSession(sessionRef string) (agent.SubagentSessionLink, bool) {
40		start, ok := readDroidSessionStart(sessionRef)
41		if !ok {
42			return agent.SubagentSessionLink{}, false
43		}
44	
45		// Both IDs are required: the parent session names the metadata directory and
46		// the tool-use ID names the task within it. A half-populated link would
47		// attribute the work to the wrong place, so treat it as a top-level session.
48		if start.CallingSessionID == "" || start.CallingToolUseID == "" {
49			return agent.SubagentSessionLink{}, false
50		}
51	
52		subagentType, description := parseDroidSessionTitle(start.SessionTitle)
53		return agent.SubagentSessionLink{
54			ParentSessionID:      start.CallingSessionID,
55			ToolUseID:            start.CallingToolUseID,
56			ParentTranscriptPath: droidSiblingTranscriptPath(sessionRef, start.CallingSessionID),
57			SubagentType:         subagentType,
58			TaskDescription:      description,
59		}, true
60	}
61	
62	// droidSiblingTranscriptPath locates another session's transcript. Droid keeps
63	// every session for a working directory as <session-id>.jsonl in one directory,
64	// so a Worker's parent is always its sibling. Returns "" when absent.
65	func droidSiblingTranscriptPath(sessionRef, sessionID string) string {
66		if sessionID == "" {
67			return ""
68		}
69		path := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(sessionRef), sessionID+".jsonl")
70		if info, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil || info.IsDir() {
71			return ""
72		}
73		return path
74	}
75	
76	// readDroidSessionStart returns the session_start entry from a Droid transcript.
77	func readDroidSessionStart(path string) (droidSessionStart, bool) {
78		file, err := os.Open(filepath.Clean(path))
79		if err != nil {
80			return droidSessionStart{}, false
81		}
82		defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()
83	
84		// ReadBytes rather than bufio.Scanner: session_start embeds the full task
85		// prompt in its title, which routinely exceeds Scanner's default line cap.
86		reader := bufio.NewReader(file)
87		for range sessionStartScanLimit {
88			lineBytes, err := reader.ReadBytes('\n')
89			if len(lineBytes) > 0 {
90				var start droidSessionStart
91				if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(bytes.TrimSpace(lineBytes), &start); jsonErr == nil &&
92					start.Type == "session_start" {
93					return start, true
94				}
95			}
96			if err != nil {
97				break
98			}
99		}
100		return droidSessionStart{}, false
101	}
102	
103	// parseDroidSessionTitle splits a Worker session title into subagent type and
104	// task description. Droid formats it as "<type>: <description>"; anything else
105	// is returned as a bare description.
106	func parseDroidSessionTitle(title string) (subagentType, description string) {
107		title = strings.TrimSpace(title)
108		if title == "" {
109			return "", ""
110		}
111		prefix, rest, found := strings.Cut(title, ":")
112		if !found {
113			return "", title
114		}
115		prefix = strings.TrimSpace(prefix)
116		rest = strings.TrimSpace(rest)
117		// A colon inside a plain sentence is not a type prefix; require a short,
118		// single-token prefix ("worker", "reviewer") to read it as one.
119		if prefix == "" || rest == "" || strings.ContainsAny(prefix, " \t") {
120			return "", title
121		}
122		return prefix, rest
123	}

| Interface | Methods | When to implement |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|
| `HookSupport` | `InstallHooks`, `UninstallHooks`, `AreHooksInstalled`, `GetSupportedHooks` | Agent uses a config file for hook registration (e.g., `settings.json`) |
| `HookHandler` | `GetHookNames` | **Required for CLI hook registration** — `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` subcommands are only created for agents implementing this interface. Typically delegates to `HookNames()`. |
| `TranscriptAnalyzer` | `GetTranscriptPosition`, `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` | You want richer checkpoints with transcript-derived file lists |

- Factory AI Droid: Plain text to stdout (displayed directly in terminal)

### `SubagentSessionResolver`

**What it enables:** Attributing a detached subagent session's turn to the parent
task invocation, as a task checkpoint under `.entire/metadata/<parent>/tasks/<tool-use-id>/`.

**Without it:** Turn-end treats the subagent's session as an ordinary top-level
session and mints a session checkpoint for it — the subagent's files land on the
shadow branch under a session the user never drove, and no task checkpoint exists.

**Implement when:** Your agent dispatches subagents as sessions of their own,
firing a full SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop cycle for each. Factory AI
Droid does this for Workers: its `PostToolUse` fires when the Worker is
*dispatched*, not when it finishes, so the worktree is still untouched at
`SubagentEnd` and only the Worker's own session boundary delimits its work.

**Do NOT implement** when subagents block the parent's turn (Claude Code's Task
tool) — the `SubagentEnd` path already bounds that work correctly.

**Method:**
- `ResolveSubagentSession(sessionRef) (SubagentSessionLink, bool)` — returns the
  parent session ID, the parent's tool-use ID, and (optionally) the parent's
  transcript path. Must return `false` for ordinary sessions and whenever the
  link cannot be read; the caller then keeps the session on the normal path.

Resolve the link from data the agent itself persists (Droid records
`callingSessionId`/`callingToolUseId` on its transcript's `session_start` line)
rather than from hook ordering, so it survives asynchronous dispatch.

### `HookSupport`

**What it enables:** `entire enable` automatically installs hooks into the agent's config file.

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(factoryai-droid): attribute Worker sessions to their parent task

Droid changed Worker dispatch from blocking to background. Its PostToolUse
hook now fires when the Worker is *launched* rather than when it finishes —
~3s after PreToolUse, against an untouched worktree — so SubagentEnd found no
file changes and skipped the task checkpoint every time.

The work was not lost, but it was misattributed. A Droid Worker runs as a full
session of its own, so its file write was captured by the ordinary turn-end
path and landed on the shadow branch under the Worker's own session ID, at
.entire/metadata/<worker-session>/ instead of
.entire/metadata/<parent>/tasks/<tool-use-id>/. Subagent work therefore
surfaced as a top-level session the user never drove.

Key the attribution off data Droid persists rather than off hook ordering: a
Worker's transcript records callingSessionId and callingToolUseId on its
session_start line. Turn-end consults the new optional SubagentSessionResolver
capability and, for a subagent session, writes a task checkpoint on the parent
instead of a session checkpoint of its own. This holds whether dispatch is
synchronous or asynchronous, and does not depend on the synthetic tool-use IDs
the CLI mints when Droid's tool hooks omit one.

Claude Code deliberately does not implement the capability — its subagents
block the parent turn, so the existing SubagentEnd path already bounds them.

Fixes the two E2E tests failing on main since 2026-08-12:
TestFactoryTaskCheckpointExistsBeforeCommit and
TestFactoryCommittedCheckpointExcludesPreExistingUntrackedFiles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
